chunks: Ahmad ibn Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: My father narrated to me, from his father Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Khath'ami, from Abu Abdillah al-Sadiq (peace be upon him). He said:

Abu Dharr (may God have mercy on him) passed by the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family), and with him was Jibra'il (peace be upon him) in the form of Dihya al-Kalbi. The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) had sought his privacy. When he saw them both together, he withdrew from them without interrupting their conversation. Jibra'il (peace be upon him) said: O Muhammad! This Abu Dharr has passed by us without greeting us. Had he greeted us, we would have returned his greeting. O Muhammad! He has a supplication that he uses, which is well-known among the people of the heavens. Ask him about it when you ascend to the heavens.

When Jibra'il (peace be upon him) ascended, Abu Dharr came to the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family). The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: What prevented you, O Abu Dharr, from greeting us when you passed by us? He said: I thought, O Messenger of God, that the one with you was Dihya al-Kalbi, and that you had sought his privacy for some of your affairs. He said: That was Jibra'il (peace be upon him), O Abu Dharr. And he said: 'Had he greeted us, we would have returned his greeting.' When Abu Dharr learned that it was Jibra'il (peace be upon him), he was overcome with regret — as much as God willed — for not having greeted. So the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said to him: What is this supplication that you supplicate with? He informed me that you have a supplication well-known in the heavens. He said: Yes, O Messenger of God, I say:
O Allah! I ask You for faith in You, and affirmation of Your Prophet, and wellness from all calamity, and thankfulness for wellness, and needlessness from the most evil of people.

key_terms.أَهْلُ السَّمَاءِ: The people/inhabitants of the heavens — angels and spiritual beings
key_terms.الْعَافِيَة: Comprehensive wellness encompassing physical, spiritual, and social wellbeing
key_terms.الْغِنَى: Needlessness, self-sufficiency, freedom from dependence on others
key_terms.دِحْيَةُ الْكَلْبِيُّ: Dihya ibn Khalifa al-Kalbi, a handsome companion of the Prophet whom Jibra'il often appeared resembling

ai.seo_question: What supplication of Abu Dharr was known to the angels in heaven?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) narrates a story about Abu Dharr, the renowned companion, who once passed by the Prophet (SAWW) while Jibra'il (AS) was with him disguised as Dihya al-Kalbi. Out of respect for their private conversation, Abu Dharr refrained from greeting them, but Jibra'il praised his etiquette and revealed that Abu Dharr had a supplication known throughout the heavens. The hadith ends with the text of that noble supplication, asking God for faith, affirmation of the Prophet, wellness, gratitude, and independence from evil people — five comprehensive spiritual blessings.
